stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: An electron enters the deflection plates horizontally with speed $v_0$. Move the $U$ slider (voltage between plates) and the $v_0$ slider, then press FIRE. Notice how the beam bends inside the field and stays straight after.
stages.concept: Inside the plates the electric field is uniform: $E = U/d$. The electron feels a constant acceleration $a = qE/m = (q/m)\,U/d$ perpendicular to $v_0$, so its path is parabolic while $x \in [0, L]$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit the three target markers on the screen. The dashed line previews the beam — tune $U$ and $v_0$, then fire. Watch out: if the exit deflection exceeds $d/2$, the electron hits a plate and never reaches the screen.
stages.concept: Screen deflection: $Y = \dfrac{(q/m)\,U\,L}{d\,v_0^{2}}\,\left(D + \tfrac{L}{2}\right)$. Y scales with $U$ and with $1/v_0^{2}$; its sign follows $U$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview. Each target shows its screen coordinate $Y$ in cm. You have exactly 3 shots — one per target. Compute $U$ (given a $v_0$ you choose) from the deflection formula on paper, set the sliders, then fire.
stages.concept: Two constraints matter: (a) $Y_{\text{screen}} = (q/m)\,U\,L\,(D + L/2)/(d\,v_0^{2})$ picks the pair $(U, v_0)$ up to a family; (b) the electron must survive the plates, $|y_{\text{exit}}| = \tfrac{1}{2}(q/m)\,|U|\,(L/v_0)^{2}/d < d/2$.

labels.tip1: move U and v₀, then FIRE
labels.tip2: use the preview line to line up each target
labels.tip3: compute U from Y and v₀, then FIRE — 3 shots, one per target
labels.peek_tip_scaling: Y scales with U/v₀². Double v₀ → quarter Y for the same U. Flip the sign of U → beam flips to the other side.
labels.peek_tip_survives: Check |y_exit| = ½ · (q/m) · |U| · (L/v₀)² / d before firing. If it exceeds d/2 the electron hits a plate.
labels.peek_tip_lever: Longer field-free region D → bigger Y at the screen for the same exit angle. Y = y_exit + (D · v_y_exit / v₀).

1.1: Move the U slider up or down — the beam bends toward whichever plate is at higher potential.
1.2: The v₀ slider changes how long the electron sits in the field. Faster v₀ = less time to bend = smaller deflection.
1.3: Try U = 0: no field, no bending. The electron sails straight through and marks the screen center.

2.1: The dashed preview shows the trajectory. Line it up with a target, then fire.
2.2: A target above center needs U > 0; below center needs U < 0. Same |Y| takes the same |U| for a given v₀.
2.3: Halving v₀ multiplies Y by four for the same U. Use v₀ as a coarse knob and U as a fine one.

3.1: Read each target's Y (in cm). Pick a v₀ you can commit to, then solve U = Y · m · d · v₀² / (q · L · (D + L/2)).
3.2: With L = 10 cm, d = 4 cm, D = 10 cm and q/m = 1.76×10¹¹ C/kg: U[V] ≈ Y[cm] · v₀[10⁷ m/s]² · 15.15.
3.3: For extreme Y, either raise v₀ (safer — |y_exit| stays small) or accept a bigger |U|. Check |y_exit| < d/2 = 2 cm before you fire.
